_filtersNote: maxMarketCapUsd raised 8M -> 12M on 2026-08-08 so the ESTABLISHED INSIDER
GEM tier ($1M-$10M+) is reachable at all. At 8M the top fifth of that band
was discarded before it ever reached the audit, which would have made the
tier quietly unable to fire on the exact tokens it names.

_note: Widens the top-10 concentration cap from maxTop10Pct (20) to 30 for
tokens with a real holder base AND real turnover. Intended to stop the
flat 20% cap from rejecting mega-runners, where a higher top-10 share
sits inside a float that is being actively traded rather than in a
bundle waiting to exit into you.
READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING IT. This widens a SAFETY gate on the strength
of two metrics a scammer can manufacture cheaply: 1h volume by wash
trading between wallets they control, holder count by dusting. Both are
precisely what someone gaming a scanner would fake, because they are
what scanners look at. Neither is evidence that the top ten will not
sell into you — only that more people are currently trading.
MEASURED AGAINST THE LAST SCANS: tokens this rule would newly admit
include BLAKJAK (24.8% top-10, 1698 holders) and Atlas (22.3%, 4323
holders). Post-mortem had them at -30.1% and -54.3% respectively, and
Victor (21.9%, 3733 holders) at -53.5%. That is three for three going
down after being caught by the 20% cap. One scan window is not a
verdict, but it is the only evidence currently on file and it points
the other way.
Both inputs must be affirmatively KNOWN — unknown holders or unknown
volume keep the base cap. Set enabled=false to restore a flat 20%.
Breaking-news correlation. MEASURED source availability:
CoinDesk / Cointelegraph / Decrypt / The Block RSS  200 [OK]   no key
CryptoPanic API                                     403 [FAIL] needs a key
So RSS is the backbone; set CRYPTOPANIC_TOKEN in .env to add CryptoPanic.
Dead sources are named in the scan log rather than silently dropped.
A match requires BOTH a watched keyword in a fresh headline AND that
keyword appearing in the token's own name or symbol. Without the second
half, every token scanned during a Binance story would be 'news matched'.
THIS ADDS NO SCORE, deliberately. A token named after a breaking story is
the signature of an opportunistic launch at least as often as a real
opportunity — someone sees the headline, mints the ticker, and sells to
whoever searches for it. The label means 'topical', never 'good'. Every
safety gate still applies, and the alert says so in the message body.
freshnessMinutes is the window between the story and the match. 3 minutes
is very tight and will match rarely; widen it if you want more flow, at
the cost of catching launches that merely followed the news rather than
front-ran it.
Search-spike tracking. MEASURED availability:
CoinGecko /search/trending   200 [OK]   no key, 15 coins
CoinGecko /coins/{id}        200 [OK]   no key, gives per-chain contracts
Twitter/X API v2             401 [FAIL] paid bearer token required
So SEARCH SPIKE is real and MENTION VELOCITY is not. Twitter code is
written and inert until TWITTER_BEARER_TOKEN is set.
MATCHING IS ON CONTRACT ADDRESS, NOT TICKER, and this matters. The
trending payload carries only name and symbol, so the obvious
implementation — compare tickers — creates the attack it is meant to
reward: mint a token called PENGU while PENGU trends, collect +20, sell
into whoever the alert reaches. Solana's ticker namespace is
unrestricted and impersonation is the default, not an edge case.
So each trending id is resolved through /coins/{id} to platforms.solana
and matched against the real mint. allowSymbolMatch re-enables ticker
matching; leave it false unless you have a reason, and note the alert
labels a symbol-only match as unverified.
Resolution costs one call per trending coin against a rate-limited free
tier, hence cacheMinutes and resolveDelayMs. Trending moves in hours;
the scanner runs every 30 seconds.
Viral-volume boost: real money through the pool plus buyers heavily
outnumbering sellers right now. Additive to the score, and forfeited
entirely unless the contract audit AFFIRMATIVELY passed — the same bar
the insider multiplier is held to, because this is the easiest bonus in
the engine to manufacture.
minBuys is not in the original specification and is deliberate: a 3:1
ratio off 3 buys and 1 sell is rounding, not demand. detectCatalysts has
paired every ratio test with a buy-count floor since the beginning, and
without one a single buy into a pool with zero sells scores an infinite
ratio. Lower it to 1 to get the unguarded behaviour.
SCORE INFLATION WARNING: +25 stacks on the insider multiplier (up to
+50), CTO (+20) and the category boost (+10). A token drawing several of
those clamps at 100, and once many tokens sit at 100 the score stops
discriminating between them and the 68 alert floor stops filtering.
Watch how many alerts arrive at 95-100 and lower scoreBoost if the
distribution flattens.
megaRunner.alertHeader: 380x MEGA-RUNNER VIRAL ALERT ($50k+ Vol & High Demand!)
_alertHeaderNote: The '380x' is a fixed string in the header, not a computed figure —
Aegis has no way to project a multiple and does not try. It will read as
'380x' on a token that goes to zero, which is most of them.
Everything else in the alert is careful about this: sell signals state
movement 'from the alert market cap, not your P&L' precisely so a number
is never mistaken for a promise. This header is the one place that
convention is broken, at explicit request. A neutral alternative:
Change this one string to switch; nothing else depends on it.

_minAbsoluteLiquidityNote: Absolute-depth alternative to minLiqToMcapPct, applied ONLY to the
ESTABLISHED INSIDER GEM tier. Added 2026-08-08 because the 15% ratio floor
rejected that entire band: real $1M-$10M tokens sit at 5-12%, so a $3.4M
token with a $410k pool scored 0 and the tier could never have fired.
It IS a loosening, and worth knowing: a $100k pool absorbs a retail exit at
single-digit slippage, but it does not make a $10M token as exitable as 15%
would. Size the exit to the pool, not to the market cap. Every other token,
the early insider tier included, still faces the full ratio floor.
_signalCategoryNote: Two holding styles. GEM requires every condition positively proven —
an unknown age or holder count disqualifies it — because its advice is to
hold for days/weeks. SCALP tolerates an unproven age since 'take profit
Measured from 453 post-mortem outcomes as of 2026-08-05:
$15k-300k (the SCALP band) failed 40% of the time (154/389),
Nothing has ever been scanned at >=$1M, so GEM will not fire until

_precedence: Four tiers, evaluated in this order — the first match wins:
3. gem                 mature and deep, no insider requirement
The insider tiers are tested FIRST and legitimately overlap the plain
ones: a mature $400k token with cluster activity becomes an EARLY-STAGE
INSIDER SCALP rather than a GEM. The insider entry is the more
decision-relevant fact, and the tighter stop is the safer of the two
pieces of advice to give about the same token.
Between the plain tiers, GEM still wins the overlap: a $300k-$1M token
that is >=12h old with >=$50k liquidity becomes a GEM, while a younger or
thinner one in the same band becomes a SCALP.
'category' is the stable machine value used by Dataview queries.
'label' is the display string shown in alerts and notes — change that

_note: Requirements shared by BOTH insider tiers. Enforced in audit.mjs by
evaluateInsiderRequirements(), which is stricter than the contract
audit in one specific way: UNKNOWN COUNTS AS FAILURE. The contract
audit reports missing provider data as UNVERIFIED and leaves the token
watchable; an insider tier is a promotion — a louder header, and score
for the established tier — so it may not rest on data that was never
returned.
Mint/freeze revoked and 'audit must be PASSED' are implicit in those
two rows and are not separately configurable: they are the definition
of a clean contract, not a tunable.
scoreFloor is the same 68 as telegram.insiderMinScore, which is the
value the notifier actually applies. It is restated here because the
floor is part of the tier definition, not just a Telegram setting.
The score cannot be checked during classification — the tier's own
scoreBoost feeds into it — so the floor is applied at dispatch.
Classification shown for a confirmed CTO. Detection thresholds live in
the top-level communityTakeover block; this is only the label, advice
and alert header.
communityTakeover.label: COMMUNITY TAKEOVER GEM
communityTakeover.advice: Community takeover — the developer has exited and the crowd is driving. No dev to rug, and no dev to build.

_note: maxMarketCapUsd is null on purpose: the tier is specified as
'$1M-$10M+', so there is no ceiling. filters.maxMarketCapUsd is what
actually bounds it, since a token above that is never scanned at all.
insiderEstablished.label: ESTABLISHED INSIDER GEM
insiderEstablished.advice: Established insider accumulation — high 90%+ survival rate & deep liquidity.

_note: scoreBoost is 0, matching the plain scalp tier. An early insider entry
already earns +15 to +50 from insiderScaleTiers; adding a band bonus on
top would let market-cap size alone push a thin token over the floor.
OPEN MISMATCH: this tier's advice says '-15% stop-loss', but the
automated SELL SIGNAL still fires at sellSignals.stopLossPct = 20, and
that setting is global rather than per-tier. So the alert text asks for
a tighter stop than the notifier will actually send. Either enforce -15
by hand, or lower sellSignals.stopLossPct — which would tighten every
position, not just this tier.
_minHoldersNote: Per-tier holder floor, replacing the global thresholds.minUniqueHolders
(150) for this tier only. Set to 75 so fresh $30k-$75k launches can
clear the gate while they still have a small holder base.
NOTE ON HOW THIS WORKS: setting this key alone would have done nothing.
Before 2026-08-09 the early tier checked market cap and nothing else,
and the 150 floor lived in scoreToken as a global safety gate. The gate
is now tier-aware via resolveHolderFloor(), and the tier itself
requires the count to be KNOWN and >= this number.
MEASURED AGAINST THE NOTE ARCHIVE at the time of the change:
<75 holders     7 graded, 7 rugged, 0 wins   -> 100% rug rate
75-149 holders  0 graded                     -> NO DATA EITHER WAY
150+ holders    2512 graded, 1946 rugged     -> 77% rug rate
So this opens a band with no evidence in it, immediately above a band
that has never once survived. The 150 floor exists because holder count
is a separate axis from concentration: ten wallets can hold a clean 8%
each and still leave a token exit-trapped because there is nobody to
sell to. Fewer holders means thinner exit liquidity, and the sub-75
record is what that looks like in practice.
Raise back to 150 (or delete this key) to restore the global floor.
Watch the post-mortem rug rate for this tier before scaling size into
it — 7 samples one band down is a warning, not a verdict, but there is
nothing on file pointing the other way.
_minInsiderWalletsNote: Requires COORDINATION, not one wallet doing something unusual. Two
conditions, both mandatory: at least 2 distinct insider wallets, AND
structural evidence tying them together — co-buying inside the 60s
launch window, a shared funding origin, or same-slot execution.
The structural half is what matters. A bare count would be satisfied
by two unrelated watchlisted wallets buying hours apart, which is not
a cabal, it is two people liking the same coin.
IMPACT, measured against the 301 insider-detected notes on file: 243
of them (81%) are NON-ROUTINE BUY SIZE with cluster size 0 and no
funder network — a single wallet making one large buy. Every one of
those is now blocked from this tier. Expect early-scalp alerts to
become rare; that is the intent, but it is a large reduction and the
flow should be watched rather than assumed.
Not applied to insiderEstablished: its own floors (>=$1M cap, >=$100k
liquidity, >=1000 holders) already exclude the launch-sniping noise
this targets. Set minInsiderWallets there too if you want it.

_note: Community Takeover detection — the $RAVECAT pattern: developer walks
away, the crowd keeps trading, and the token survives without them.
All four criteria must pass. None is meaningful alone: holders can be
sybilled, volume can be washed, and a dev can move funds to a second
wallet and look 'exited'. Together they are decent evidence, and they
are treated as evidence rather than proof.
maxDevBalancePct is read from chain (the creator's live token balance as
a share of supply), NOT from a provider flag, and only after the three
free criteria pass — so the extra RPC call costs nothing on tokens that
were never candidates. An unreadable balance FAILS the criterion: 'we
could not find the dev's balance' is not 'the dev has gone'.
WHAT A CONFIRMED CTO OVERRIDES: the dev-exit penalty (creator-sold risk
flags stop counting, since a departed dev is the premise) and the
liquidity depth RATIO, replaced by the $100k absolute floor in
thresholds.minAbsoluteLiquidityUsd.
WHAT IT NEVER OVERRIDES: mint authority, freeze authority, LP burn,
top-10 concentration, the 150-holder floor, or a SERIAL RUGGER deployer.
A crowd cannot revoke an authority the developer kept, and 'the
community took it over' is exactly the story that would be told to
launder a rugger's token.
Three pillars, adapted from the equities cluster-buying idea. The
adaptation is weaker by nature: equities insiders are named in mandatory
filings, on-chain ones are inferred from behaviour.
PILLAR 1 cluster   — 2+ tracked or co-funded wallets buying inside the
launch window. One buyer is noise; several together
within seconds is coordination.
PILLAR 2 sizing    — a single buy over 5 SOL or over 5% of the pool.
Size cannot be faked.
PILLAR 3 funder    — wallets whose FIRST funding shares a source. Verified
working against Helius: a fresh wallet's earliest
transaction reveals both funder and amount.
LIMITS: funder tracing only reaches wallets with <1000 lifetime
signatures (RPC page limit), which excludes established traders — fine,
since cabal wallets are purpose-made and fresh. A shared funder is often
just a CEX hot wallet, so it is reported but scored only lightly and
never treated as proof of insider knowledge.
_scalingNote: Multi-insider scaling multiplier, keyed on the count of DISTINCT insider
wallets. The three detection sources overlap heavily — one wallet can be
watchlisted AND early AND co-funded — so the count is of unique addresses,
not list lengths, or a single wallet would score as three.
Applied ONLY after every safety gate passes. audit.mjs zeroes this on any
gate failure, so a cabal buying its own rug can never outscore a clean
ADDITIVE to the fundamentals, not a floor: a swarm lands at base+50
clamped to 100. A token with weak demand and thin liquidity will not
reach 90 on insider count alone — four wallets buying something illiquid
is a reason to look, not a reason to override the market data.
_jitoBundleNote: PILLAR 4 — same-slot co-execution, the on-chain fingerprint of a Jito
bundle. Transactions in one bundle execute atomically and land in the
same slot; standard RPC exposes the slot but NOT a bundle id, so the
slot match is the strongest thing derivable without a second provider.
It is genuinely strong: a Solana slot is ~400ms, and several fresh
wallets independently choosing to buy a minutes-old token inside the
same 400ms is not plausible coincidence. It is not conclusive — a busy
slot on a hot launch can hold unrelated buyers — which is why the
threshold is 3 wallets rather than 2, and why the boost is forfeited on
any safety-gate failure like every other multiplier.
confirmViaJitoApi upgrades 'same slot' to 'confirmed bundle' by asking
bundles.jito.wtf which bundle a signature belongs to. That endpoint is
live and answers with structured JSON, but it is a third party outside
this pipeline, so it is best-effort: a timeout or an error downgrades
the result to 'same slot, unconfirmed' instead of discarding it. Costs
up to maxBundleLookups HTTP calls, and only on tokens that already have
a slot match.
Unlike the funder trace, slot analysis runs on EVERY buyer rather than
being gated behind a watchlist hit — a bundle of three fresh wallets is
precisely the case where none of them is watchlisted yet, so gating it
would blind the tracer to the cabals it exists to catch. It needs no
extra RPC: the slot arrives with the signature listing.

_note: Jito validator tip analysis. Sums the SOL paid to Jito's tip accounts by
the transactions in a token's launch window — what a cabal paid for
guaranteed, ordered inclusion at launch.
WHAT THIS SIGNAL IS. Intent and capital, measured in SOL. Nobody tips 5
SOL to buy a token casually: whoever paid it needed to be first, in a
specific slot, badly enough to burn real money on the ordering alone, and
had the money to burn before the position was open.
WHAT IT IS NOT, and this is the important half. A tip is the ONE signal in
this engine that is purchased outright rather than earned. Every other
multiplier needs something done — wallets acquired, size moved, volume
generated. This one needs a payment, to a public address, that anybody
can make. Five SOL buys a '5 SOL tip' and nothing else.
THE MISREAD THAT COSTS MONEY: a developer rugging their own launch has
exactly the same incentive to tip. They want their own buys sequenced
ahead of the crowd's, and the tip is a rounding error against what they
intend to extract. A large tip on a token whose LP is not burned is
evidence of a WELL-FUNDED operation — a reason for more suspicion, not
less. The bonus is therefore forfeited unless the contract audit
affirmatively PASSED, the same bar the mega-runner boost is held to.
COST: normally zero extra RPC. Buyer replay in smart_money.mjs already
fetches every launch transaction, so the tip is read from a response
already in memory. maxSignatureLookups bounds the fallback path used when
a buyer row arrives without one.
launchWindowSeconds scopes the sum to the launch. A tip on an ordinary
trade an hour later is someone paying for priority in a busy market,
which is a different fact and should not inflate the same number. A buyer
whose launch offset is UNKNOWN is excluded rather than assumed to be in
the window — pair creation time is often missing on bonding-curve pairs,
and assuming would turn 'all buyers' into 'launch buyers' on exactly the
tokens where the distinction matters most.
refreshTipAccounts re-reads the account list from Jito's block engine at
runtime, unioned with the eight pinned in bundle_tracer.mjs (read from
that endpoint and verified against chain on 2026-08-09). It is additive
and never subtractive: a wrong or missing tip account reports every token
as untipped, which reads as a measurement rather than a broken lookup.
Set false to use the pinned list only and make no third-party call.
DexScreener has no trending endpoint (403/404 on every variant). The
boost/profile feeds skew tiny — measured 0 pairs above $1M. The search
endpoint skews the opposite way, so both are used and unioned.
Measured yield per query into the $300k-$8M band: solana=13, SOL=4,
dog=2, pump/cat/AI/trump=1 each, meme/moon/WIF=0.

_insiderBypassNote: HIGH-CONVICTION INSIDER ANTI-RUG BYPASS. This is a switch that turns OFF
safety checks. Read the whole note before leaving it on.
WHAT IT DOES. When a matched insider carries a score >= the floor, three
gates stop blocking that token: LP burn/lock, top-10 concentration, and
the unique-holder floor (global AND the per-tier one). The token is then
scored, classified into an insider tier and alerted as though those gates
had passed, and the alert carries a HIGH-RISK NOTICE naming each waived
gate with its real measured value.
WHAT IT CANNOT REACH, by construction, not by configuration:
mint authority, freeze authority, rug/danger flags, a SERIAL RUGGER
deployer, the blacklist, and liquidity depth. Also UNVERIFIED audits —
the override clears gates that FAILED on known data, never gates that
could not be checked. And a token failing a bypassable gate AND a
non-bypassable one is not bypassed at all.
WHAT YOU ARE TRADING AWAY, plainly. An unburned LP is the developer still
holding the ability to withdraw the pool. A concentrated top 10 is the
list of wallets that will be selling into you. A thin holder base is the
absence of anyone to sell to when you want out. A high-scoring buyer
changes none of the three — it is a fact about the buyer, not about the
contract.
THIS OPENS AN ATTACK THE REST OF THE ENGINE WAS BUILT TO CLOSE. audit.mjs
states it directly at the security-first gate: a malicious dev can buy
their own scam from a wallet on an alpha list, and if that could lift the
verdict it would be a way to walk a rug past the audit. Every bonus in the
engine — smart money, cluster, mega-runner, social hype — is forfeited on
a gate failure for exactly this reason. This switch is the exception.
ON THE FLOOR ITSELF. The score is multiplier_engine alpha points, which
are awarded at pointsPerMultiplier (2.5) per x of a harvested recap win
and then moved by forward results (+5 win, -8 loss, floor -50). So 85
means roughly a 34x launch buy, or a smaller win plus a good forward run.
That is a real bar and a small population. But those points are awarded
BECAUSE a wallet was present at a token that won — selection on the
outcome — and multiplierEngine._note explains at length why that is a
reason to watch a wallet rather than evidence about it. A wallet can also
carry a hand-set 'score' field in smart_wallets.json; a wallet with no
score at all is null and never clears the floor.
Set allowInsiderSafetyBypass to false to restore the normal behaviour: the
gates are absolute and no score overrides them. Raising
insiderBypassScoreFloor narrows how many wallets can trigger it; there is
no setting that makes a bypassed token as safe as an unbypassed one.

_note: Guards against system accounts masquerading as whales.
maxWalletSol catches exchange vaults (one held 10.7M SOL).
maxTokenAccounts catches DEX pool authorities, which hold trivial SOL
but own millions of token accounts — Raydium Authority V4 owns 1,416,453.
A balance check alone would wave those straight through.
Composite Elite Ranking. All three rules must pass — they are AND, not a
weighted blend, so a small-sample 100% win rate cannot buy a place.
No provider serves the ranking data: GMGN 403s behind Cloudflare, Birdeye
and Dune 401 without a paid key, Cielo's public feed is empty, Solscan
refuses connections. So the list is EARNED from Aegis's own observations
(buyer replay + post-mortem grading) rather than fetched. Seed it instantly
with:  node auto_top_whales.mjs --import <leaderboard.csv>
syncIntervalHours = 2: re-ranks win rates and rewrites smart_wallets.json
every 2h during the normal 12-minute scan. The ledger itself updates on
EVERY scan (buys recorded, outcomes graded) — this interval only controls
how often the ranking is recomputed and the watchlist file rewritten.
_enrichShortlistCapNote: Hard ceiling on how many wallets get per-wallet RPC work (system-account
screening, then lifetime-signature enrichment) during a sync.
Added 2026-08-08 after the ledger reached 3,444 eligible wallets.
Measured at 111 KB and 0.44s per wallet, that was ~390 MB of JSON and
~25 minutes per sync — to write topN=5 entries. On a 10-minute
maintenance cadence the loop spent most of its life syncing rather than
scanning, which is what produced the 468 skipped ticks in the logs.
50 sits far above where real candidates live: recurrence collapses 3-4x
per level (1466 wallets at >=1 graded buy, 36 at >=2, 9 at >=3). The
cost is that a wallet outside the top 50 by observation count cannot be
enriched, so it cannot pass the lifetime-trades rule. Raise this if the
ledger ever grows enough that genuine candidates sit below the cut.
Safety is unaffected: pool authorities are kept off the written list by
the SECOND screening pass, which runs over the ranked finalists and is
bounded by topN rather than by this cap.
_option2Note: Top-5 Earned Whales. minGradedBuys lowered 10 -> 3 because the ledger
showed 0 wallets could ever reach 10: a wallet cannot hold more graded
buys than there are decided tokens, and recurrence collapses 3-4x per
level (1466 wallets at >=1, 36 at >=2, 9 at >=3, 2 at >=5).
profitRule is 'skip' because nothing writes otherwise — lifetime realized
P&L is not derivable from observation. Ranking is therefore on win rate +
on-chain activity only. Imported leaderboards still carry real P&L.
SAMPLE-SIZE WARNING: at minGradedBuys=3 with a 75% win-rate bar, a wallet
with exactly 3 graded buys must be 3/3 perfect (2/3 = 66.7% fails). So the
first entries are near-perfect records over very few trades. Treat these
as candidates to watch, not proven edge, until their graded counts grow.

_insiderTiersOnlyNote: Restricts alerts to the two named tiers, so every notification carries
one of the two headers and a market-cap band you chose deliberately.
KNOWN GAP, stated rather than hidden: the tiers do not cover $12k-$30k
or $500k-$1M. An insider-backed token in either of those windows now
scores and writes a note as before but sends NO Telegram alert, where
previously it would have. Set this to false to restore alerts on every
insider-detected token regardless of band, or widen insiderEarly's
maxMarketCapUsd to 1000000 to close the upper gap.
_scorecardNote: Rolling window for the per-insider scorecard shown in BUY alerts.
WHAT IT CAN AND CANNOT SHOW. The win rate is real but is computed over
AEGIS-OBSERVED buys only — the tokens this scanner happened to scan —
not the wallet's market-wide record, and the sample skews optimistic
because buyer replay reads tokens with a live pool. Profit is ESTIMATED
(spend x later price change, assuming the wallet still holds); Aegis
never observes exits, so realized P&L is not derivable.
AVERAGE HOLDING DURATION IS NOT SHOWN. Nothing in the pipeline records
an exit timestamp, so it cannot be computed. It is omitted rather than
approximated, because a plausible number there would be invented.
Real 30-day win rate, realized P&L and holding time are what GMGN and
Birdeye sell, and both are gated (403 Cloudflare / 401 without a paid
key) — verified repeatedly, see the networkDiscovery notes. The alert
links out to them for exactly this reason.
_insiderMinScoreNote: Set to 68 on 2026-08-08 after measuring against the overnight run.
Of the 10 alerts sent that night, 5 clear 68 (scores 68-76) and 5 fall
below (45-67). A 75 floor left only 1. 68 targets ~3-5 alerts/day.
Raise toward 75 for near-silence, lower toward 60 to roughly double flow.
_silenceNote: insiderOnly=true: Telegram receives a message ONLY when a token has
insider/cluster activity AND clears every safety gate. No digests, no
scam lists, no empty-scan summaries — a tick that finds nothing sends
This REPLACES the old BUY SIGNAL + minScore rule rather than adding to
it. Real insider entries frequently sit at WATCH because the 5m demand
ratio is under 2x at the moment of entry; requiring both would filter
out exactly the early buys this mode exists to catch.
sendScanDigest forced to false — it was the only remaining source of
routine noise. Set insiderOnly=false to restore the previous behaviour.

_note: What each named source actually contributes:
Solscan  — API is key-gated, so origin tracing runs against Solana RPC
directly (same data, no key). Solscan is used for links.
Bubblemaps — no public API. Its graph is reproducible from chain:
wallets sharing a funding origin. That is computed here.
GMGN     — 403 Cloudflare. Win rate / PnL / trade count CANNOT be
Birdeye  — 401 without a paid key.      fetched. Verified repeatedly.
So discovered wallets carry deep links to GMGN and Birdeye rather than
fabricated stats. Tap through for the numbers.
EXPANSION SAFETY — maxFunderDegree is the important one. A CEX hot wallet
funds thousands of unrelated users; without this guard the net would
enrol half of Solana in a day and every token would 'match smart money'.
Expansion also only proceeds from a cluster already containing a tracked
wallet, and results go to discovered_wallets.json — NOT smart_wallets.json,
which auto_top_whales.mjs rewrites wholesale every 2h and would erase.
Positions open when a BUY alert is delivered, capturing the market cap at
that moment and each insider's token balance. Those baselines are what the
triggers measure against.
Each trigger fires AT MOST ONCE per position — otherwise a token sitting
at -21% would re-send a stop-loss every 30 seconds.
STOP_LOSS and INSIDER_EXIT close the position. TAKE_PROFIT does NOT: its
advice is to remove initial capital and let the rest run, so the stop-loss
must stay armed on the remainder.
A delisted pair counts as a stop-loss, not missing data. Liquidity being
pulled is the most important thing to be told about.
IMPORTANT: percentages are movement from the ALERT market cap, not your
P&L. Aegis does not know your fill, your size, or whether you took the
trade at all.
Emergency exit on a sharp fall in the pool's SOL reserve, read from
DexScreener's liquidity.quote — already fetched for pricing, so it
costs no extra call.
ON THE 10-SECOND WINDOW IN THE SPEC: it is not achievable here. This
monitor runs on the scan loop, whose tick targets 30s but measures
40-195s in practice, so there is no sample inside a 10-second window.
What is implemented is '>dropPct between consecutive samples', and the
alert states the REAL elapsed time rather than a configured one. A
drain caught 90s apart is still worth knowing; calling it '10s' would
fabricate precision in exactly the number used to judge urgency.
For genuine 10-second resolution the reserve must be polled on its own
timer, independent of the scan — a separate process, not a config
change. maxSampleAgeSeconds discards comparisons too stale to mean
anything: a 20-minute-old baseline says the token got quieter, not
that someone pulled the pool.
Evaluated FIRST and short-circuiting: a pool being emptied outranks
every other trigger, including a trailing lock that would otherwise
report a tidy profitable exit on a token you cannot sell.
Tiered trailing profit lock. Once a position's PEAK clears a tier, the
exit floor rises to that tier's lockGainPct, expressed as a percentage
above the alert market cap.
peak +50%  -> floor +20%
peak +100% -> floor +60%
The armed level is derived from peakMarketCap on every check rather
than stored, so the ratchet is free: the peak only rises, so the floor
can only rise. No migration onto existing positions, and no way for a
restart or a mid-trade config edit to walk a lock back down.
An armed trailing lock SUPPRESSES the fixed stop-loss, because the lock
sits above entry and the fixed stop below it — firing both would send
two alerts for one exit, the second reporting a loss on a trade that
closed in profit. A DELISTED pair is the exception and still reports
through the stop-loss: liquidity being pulled is not a profitable exit.
This is measurement of the token, not of your position. Aegis does not
know your fill, so '+20% locked' means the market cap is 20% above
where the alert fired, not that you made 20%.

_stopLossByCategoryNote: Resolves a contradiction shipped on 2026-08-08: the early-tier advice
text says 'enforce tight -15% stop-loss' while stopLossPct was a global
20, so the alert asked for a tighter stop than the notifier would send.
The category is captured on the position when the BUY alert fires, so a
position keeps the stop it was opened under even if this config changes
underneath it. Anything not listed here uses stopLossPct.
_takeProfitNote: Lowered 2.0 -> 1.5 on 2026-08-08 from measured behaviour, not preference.
Across 10 overnight positions: 8 hit STOP_LOSS, 0 hit TAKE_PROFIT, median
peak +56%. Five peaked between +56% and +99% and then round-tripped past
-20%. $NEEGY peaked at +99% — one point short of the 2x trigger.
At 1.5x those same five fire near their highs: 5/10 instead of 0/10.

_note: Channel listener (telegram_listener.mjs). Reads public signal channels
over MTProto and feeds any Solana mint it sees into the ordinary audit
pipeline.
SECURITY MODEL: channel text is DATA, never instruction. The listener
extracts base58 mints with a regex and discards everything else — it
does not follow links, act on commands, or trust any claim a channel
makes about a token. Every address goes through the same audit, shield
and insider pipeline as a discovered one, so a channel posting a rug
gets the rug verdict, not an alert.
requiresLogin: MTProto needs a USER session, not a bot token — bots
cannot read channels they do not administer. Run 'node
telegram_listener.mjs --login' yourself to produce a session string;
it asks for your phone, an SMS code and your 2FA password. Nobody else
should ever run that for you, and the session string it prints grants
full access to your Telegram account — treat it like a password.
channels: @usernames, t.me links or numeric ids. An empty list means
the listener watches every chat the session can see, which is noisy;
name the channels you actually want.
Cadence for loop.mjs. 30s is the TARGET, not the achieved rate: a full
pass measured 40-55s, and discovery is a fixed cost that does not shrink
with scanLimit. The loop skips a tick when the previous scan is still
running, so the real cadence tracks scan duration and skipped ticks are
reported rather than hidden.
To get closer to 30s: lower scanLimit and trim discovery.searchQueries.
RPC BUDGET: this runs ~2000 scans/day vs ~120 on the 12-minute task.
Turns a channel recap win into a watchlist of launch buyers, then tests
them forward.
THE STATISTICAL WARNING THAT MATTERS MOST. These wallets are selected
BECAUSE they were in a token that won — selection on the outcome, which
on its own establishes nothing. Every buyer of a 42x looks brilliant
afterwards, including the ones who bought a hundred rugs the same week
and never appear in a recap. Recap channels compound it by publishing
winners and omitting losers, so the input is a biased sample of a biased
sample.
An alpha score is therefore a REASON TO WATCH a wallet, not evidence
about it. The forward record is what converts one into the other: every
later graded buy awards forwardWinPoints or deducts forwardLossPoints,
so a wallet that got lucky once decays instead of keeping a permanent
credential. Loss points exceed win points on purpose — the measured base
rate is ~77% rugged, so symmetric scoring would drift upward on noise.
COST CONTROL: harvesting walks the pool back to genesis, which on a token
that ran 42x is tens of pages before a single transaction is fetched.
minMultiplierToHarvest keeps that walk off small recaps, genesisMaxPages
bounds it, and requireGenesis refuses to credit launch-buyer alpha when
the cap was hit — a partial walk finds buyers who are early-ish, not
early, and crediting them fills the protected list with latecomers.
MEASURED on $RAVECAT (42x): 25 pages did NOT reach genesis and the
engine correctly refused to credit; 250 pages reached it in 69 pages and
53 seconds. 25 was far too low to harvest the exact tokens this targets.
KNOWN LIMITATION — POOL GENESIS IS NOT TOKEN LAUNCH. For a pump.fun
token that graduated, the Raydium/pumpswap pool is CREATED at migration,
so walking it back finds migration-era buyers, not the bonding-curve
buyers who entered before it. Those earlier trades went through the
bonding-curve program and are invisible to a pool walk entirely.
The same RAVECAT run returned 4 genesis buyers, ALL of them without an
attributable entry price — the first transactions on a fresh pool are
liquidity operations rather than ordinary swaps, so filterLaunchWindow
excluded every one. That is the guard working, but it means the harvest
will often credit nobody on graduated tokens. Reaching true launch buyers
requires replaying the bonding-curve program, which is a different
traversal and is not implemented here.
mega_win_protected wallets survive pruneObservations even with zero
surviving buys. The whole point of tracking them is what they do NEXT,
which can be months away, so ageing them out would discard the record
exactly while waiting for the thing it exists for. Their buy history
still ages normally; only the wallet row and its score persist.
Conviction ladder mapping score to a recommended SOL size, rendered as a
bold line in every BUY alert.
ON THE NAME: this is a fixed ladder, NOT the Kelly criterion. Kelly is
f* = (bp - q)/b and needs a win probability and a payoff ratio; neither
exists at the moment of alert. The nearest measured input is the
post-mortem base rate — currently ~77% rugged across 2,500+ graded
tokens — and fed to Kelly honestly that returns a NEGATIVE fraction,
i.e. 'do not size this'. The ladder is a deliberate human override of
that arithmetic, which is a legitimate choice, but it is not a derived
optimum and should not be described as one.
WHAT THE LADDER DOES NOT KNOW: your bankroll, your open exposure, or
pool depth. 2 SOL into an 800 SOL pool is nothing; 2 SOL into a 12 SOL
pool is most of the float and moves the price against you on the way in
AND on the way out. The alert therefore prints the size as a percentage
of the pool, and warns above thinPoolWarnPct — it does NOT shrink the
size, because the number you configured is the number you get.
The top rung is reached on score alone. Cabal Swarm and Jito Block #0
decorate its label rather than gating it, so a 95 earned on clean
fundamentals is not silently sized like a 75.
Watches for 429s and quota-exhaustion bodies from Helius, CoinGecko,
RugCheck and DexScreener, and sends one Telegram warning per provider
per cooldown window.
WHY IT EXISTS: a throttled key does not announce itself, it degrades
quietly. The whale sync derived 48/48 PnL figures on one run and 22/48
an hour later purely from request pacing, and the CoinGecko resolver
recorded WIF, JUP and BONK as not-a-Solana-token when its lookups 429d.
Both kept running and produced a worse answer that looked exactly like a
normal one. That silent loss of fidelity is what this catches.
minEventsToAlert exists because a single 429 is ordinary backpressure
that self-corrects; alerting on it would train the alert to be ignored.
An EXHAUSTED classification (a quota message in the body, or HTTP 402)
alerts on the first occurrence regardless — that one does not recover on
its own and needs a new key.
The cooldown is persisted to .state/ because every scan is a fresh
process; an in-memory guard would re-alert on every single run.

_auditConcurrencyNote: How many tokens are ANALYSED at once. Only the analysis is parallel — it is
network-bound (security fetch, buyer replay, deployer audit, funder
tracing) and that is where the ~27s per token goes.
Side effects stay SEQUENTIAL and in candidate order: notes, alerts,
positions, the digest and the console log. Parallelising those buys
nothing and breaks things that matter — interleaved log lines,
nondeterministic digest ordering, and check-then-act races across awaits
in the alert cooldown and the position opener.
RAISING THIS MULTIPLIES RPC PRESSURE by the same factor. Helius already
429s under load in this pipeline (measured in the whale sync and the
CoinGecko resolver), so 4 is deliberately modest. If audits start failing
or buyer replays come back empty, lower it before anything else.
_auditCooldownNote: Audit cooldown shield. A mint audited within this window is skipped when
selecting candidates, so each tick spends its budget on tokens it has not
WHY IT MATTERS: discovery surfaces ~130 candidates and the scan audits
6-10, sorted by 1h volume. That sort barely changes between ticks, so
without a cooldown the same handful is re-audited every ~50 seconds while
~120 others are never looked at once.
WHAT IT COSTS: a token audited at 60/100 that becomes a 90 two minutes
later is not re-scored for up to 10 minutes, so its alert is delayed by
that much. Worth it only because the never-seen pile is ~12x larger than
the seen one. Lower this if you would rather re-check known movers often;
raise it to widen coverage further.
